chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Playing for Mexican and gypsy dances in the 1920s
summary: Ethnic groups kept to themselves; Spikes remembers selling papers at the Plaza and, with the music store, playing jazz for Mexican and gypsy dances in Boyle Heights.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Well, I don't know when it ever got that way because I never had any trouble but look at all the other races. Look at Japanese. They all segregate themselves. And Chinatown, when it was all down where the Union Station was. When I was a child, I used to sell papers all down in there. At the Plaza, I sold papers in '97 and '98 and '99--all through there--I sold papers at the Plaza, and I'd go from the Times Building--then the Record Building--and go up Spring and Broadway...uh, Spring and Main Street till I got to the Plaza, and I had two, three customers in there, and then I'd come all back down, and I sold papers, mostly my corner was Third and Main Street And you take a...you look at the Mexicans. They all got... they all do that. Just like when I had the music store, I used to play for a lot of gypsies. They had the big celebrations, and they was all the way out in Boyle Heights, way out by the cemetery, and

we'd go out there on Sundays and play and they all be dancing and everything and there with the Negro band. We had a lot fun. We used to play for all of them. Used to play for nearly all of the Mexican dances.
No. You know those young kids don't want no Mexican music. They wanted jazz!
How about the gypsies? Uh...did any of them play any kind of a gypsy music?
They didn't while we was there. They wanted us to play.
Yeahhhh. We played for them lots of times on ...and the Mexicans we played regular, a couple nights a week different places, and they wanted the jazz, that's what they wanted...
The period you were doing all this was what period--around what year?
